title: CPlane Bridgeplaybook — Standup notes and handover checklist
content:
Context:
This is a lightweight week-of handover/standup note for the control plane team focusing on routing, auth, and quota behaviors. The goal is to capture the 'bridgeplaybook' items that ops/oncall or a receiving squad needs to know during sprint turnover or short-term escalations. Keep this doc short — link out to runbooks for details.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Routing: small routing policy regression observed in canary around 08/17 causing fallback to default-tier for ~30m; mitigated by forcing route-cache invalidation and reverting policy commit. Root cause: stale rule precedence ordering in allocator.
- Auth: rolling token rotation for dedicated-controlplane completed (new KMS key); minor spike in 500s from stale client certs — we have a short script to nudge clients.
- Quotas: new quota fallthrough test (sim-scenario B) surfaced an edgecase where per-customer burst window overlaps global soft-limit leading to premature throttling.

What we discussed in standup (08/19):
1) Routing policy regression followup
   - Symptoms: requests to model variants with "latency-preferred" tag were routed to default pool for 08:12-08:42 UTC. 95p latency and token cost stayed flat.
   - Immediate mitigation: revert routing policy commit (PR #411), clear route-cache on affected allocators, restart router-proxy on 3 nodes.
   - Root cause hypothesis: policy compiler emitted precedence numbers with rounding collision for policies with identical priority buckets.
   - Short-term fix: patch policy-compiler to include tie-breaker (policy GUID) in precedence sort.
   - Longer term: add unit test for precedence collisions and a canary that validates route mapping for ~500 synthetic requests per canary run.

2) Auth token rotation and client nudging
   - Status: rotation done; KMS key swapped at 06:00 UTC on 08/18.
   - Observed: ~0.3% 500s from older client certs that didn't refresh.
   - Action: run client-nudge for stale certs (script: tools/auth/client-nudge.sh). Notify Solutions Eng to push update to customers with long-lived SDKs.

3) Quota fallthrough edgecase
   - Test: sim-scenario B (overlapping burst window) run against staging quotas surfaced that global soft-limit enforcement can preempt per-customer burst allowance when intervals align.
   - Impact: small set of internal synthetic workloads failed with 429s in a narrow time window.
   - Mitigation: change enforcement order so customer bursts are applied prior to global soft-limit; requires careful race handling.
   - Owner: Samir to prototype change and run against canary traffic by EOW.

4) Observability gaps called out
   - Missing metric: route-policy-compiler.last-success-hash (hard to correlate bad deploys to compiler outputs).
   - Missing alert: quota-enforcement-mismatch (when per-customer counters differ from global view).
   - Quick wins: add compiler hash to deployment events; add a low-noise anomaly detector for quota drift.

Decisions made
- Ship precedence tie-breaker in policy-compiler as a hotfix (PR target: 08/20).
- Quota enforcement order change will be prototyped in branch and validated in canary before merging.
- Add compiler hash to deployment event payloads (simple change, roll out this sprint).

Open questions / things to watch
- Could the tie-breaker hide an underlying policy-spec problem (too many similar priority rules)? We should escalate to Policy UX for stricter validation in the editor.
- Client SDKs with manual cert refresh: how many customers are on this path? Solutions Eng to provide list.
- Canary coverage: are our synthetic mappings actually exercising the more complex policy permutations? We might need a small corpus of 10k synthetic routes.

Action items (owner + due):
- Patch policy-compiler to add GUID tie-breaker + tests (Marco) — due 2026-08-20 — JIRA-PLTFM-1729
- Run client-nudge and send customer-facing note (Elena) — due 2026-08-20 — slack #cs-cust-alerts
- Prototype quota enforcement re-ordering in staging (Samir) — due 2026-08-23 — JIRA-PLTFM-1745
- Add route-compiler hash to deployment events (Noah) — due 2026-08-21 — github PR planned
- Add canary test that verifies route mapping for 500 synthetic routes (Aisha) — due 2026-08-26

Quick playbook for oncall (short checklist):
- If routing regression seen: 1) check compiler hash against last successful; 2) roll-back last policy PR; 3) clear route cache on affected allocators; 4) restart router-proxy on minimal nodes.
- If auth spike: check key-rotation timeline, run client-nudge, check cert refresh logs.
- If quota 429s spike: check per-customer counters and global counters; if mismatch, temporarily relax global soft-limit and run sim-scenario B to verify.

Notes and links:
- Confluence (bridgeplaybook draft): CONFLUENCE-3852
- Relevant PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/pltfm-controlplane/pull/411, /pull/414
- Simulation harness: internal-tools/quota-sim (branch: sim-scenario-B)
- Slack thread: #platform-routing | message ids: 48732..48746

Retro / learnings from this week:
- Small compiler invariants cause outsized risk; we need better pre-deploy fuzzing of policy outputs.
- Canary traffic needs to include deterministic route mapping assertions, not just a smoke pass.
- A short 'nudge' utility for client certs is low-cost and should be integrated into the rotation playbook.

Appendix (scratch):
- notes-to-self: write small script that maps policy inputs -> stable priority tuple (priority, creation-timestamp, GUID) so sorting is deterministic.
- quick commands: 
    - clear route cache: tools/ops/route-cache-clear --allocator <id>
    - restart router-proxy: kubectl rollout restart deployment/router-proxy -n controlplane
    - run client-nudge: tools/auth/client-nudge.sh --since 2026-07-01

If you're picking this up for handover: start with 'action items' above, then validate the compiler hash on the last 3 deploys before touching runtime nodes. Flag any gaps here and ping me (Aisha) in slack.

-- Aisha
